skills_considered.reason: The reading route for the paper itself; the per-paper pipeline M0-M5 of the standing brief is its structure.

Not needed. The Europe PMC OA route returned 404 because the article is a NIHPA author manuscript outside the OA subset, but NCBI E-utilities efetch returned complete JATS XML with body, figures, tables and references, and the supplement came from the PMC binary route through pmc_pow_fetch.py. The cascade this skill exists to run was not reached.

NOT TRIGGERED, and the determination was made mechanically rather than assumed. All 18 consolidated baseline claims were enumerated from claim_registry_current.md and read: every one concerns WWOX-DEE neurobiology (network excitability, myelination, GABAergic interneurons, P47T, WOREE/SCAR12, prenatal cortex, Q230P, WW-domain cooperativity). None concerns osteosarcoma, RUNX2, bone tumour biology or tumour-suppression restoration. PMID 20530675 is CORPUS P268 with Claim links: none. The reading therefore narrows, reverses, corroborates and removes nothing on a consolidated baseline claim and justifies no MAJOR working-model bump. The one canonical surface it touches is the qualification note under CLAIM 036, whose Status is in observation.

Applied in the reading rather than as a separate pass: the mRNA/protein discordance in SAOS-2 is recorded as a discovery lead because it is the turnover-versus-transcription question the repository has already paid for once.

Declined. Nothing here matures a therapeutic lever for the reference genotype. The only intervention tested is WWOX re-expression in tumour lines, whose transfer to a germline WWOX-DEE genotype is T3, and the paper contains no molecule, dose or endpoint that a hypothesis could be built on.
Declined. No molecule is promoted by this reading; BLOCK-1 has no object.
Declined. The matrix orders a batch; this is a single assigned PMID whose position in the lot was fixed by the dispatch.

group_assessment.weighting: Senior author Rami I. Aqeilan; the counts are the repository measurement of 2026-08-11 carried forward (Aqeilan RI[Author] 137 records, with WWOX in title/abstract 64) and were not re-derived today. This is a primary WWOX laboratory and NOT a primary group for the WWOX-DEE clinical phenotype, so the two halves of the paper are weighted differently. First-hand weight: the immunohistochemistry, the cell-line panels, the xenografts and the mouse bone work, which are this lab's own reagents and models — the anti-WWOX antiserum and the Ad-WWOX virus are acknowledged gifts from Huebner and Fabbri. Reduced weight: every step that carries a bone-tumour observation toward disease-level interpretation, and in particular the RUNX2 axis, where the interpretive frame comes from the same lab's own reference 8 and is here tested against human tissue for the first time — and fails. The co-authors Gary Stein, Janet Stein and Jane Lian are a primary RUNX2/bone group, which strengthens the bone-biology reading and does not extend to the WWOX-DEE transfer question. This is an oncology paper: under gold_is_in_the_details rule 3 the disease context is not a reason to downgrade it, and it is read in full for that reason, but nothing in it is a WWOX-DEE allele.

field_density.note: The WWOX-RUNX2 intersection is a twelve-record field and this paper is one of its foundations, which is why its human-tissue negative matters more than its size suggests: there is no large literature to average it against. The WWOX AND osteosarcoma count of 28 is unchanged from the 2026-08-11 measurement.

multihop.note: All 36 references were enumerated from the XML with their PMIDs; the list is complete, not sampled. Exactly two carry a complete_fulltext_read receipt in this repository, both from this same laboratory: 17360458 (Targeted deletion of Wwox) and 18487609 (WWOX essential for post-natal survival and normal bone metabolism). Those two are precisely the sources this paper leans on hardest — reference 7 supplies the ~30% osteosarcoma incidence that this paper revises to 100%, and reference 8 supplies the entire WWOX-RUNX2 interaction premise — so the two load-bearing hops are read rather than assumed. Queued and named rather than silently dropped: 18931939 (Nathan 2009), which is both the source of the RUNX2 antibody and the premise that RUNX2 is elevated in osteosarcoma, and 16223882 (Fabbri 2005), the source of the Ad-WWOX construct, which is already assigned to this same actor in a later wave of AQEILAN-FT-C-001.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where does PMID 20530675 already occur in the disease model, what identity does each occurrence carry, and does this reading touch a consolidated baseline claim?
corpus_crossquery.note: Eight files answered. paper_registry_current.md (CORPUS P268) and literature_tracking_log_current.md (LIT-0268) carry the CORRECT identity — Cancer Res, DOI 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-09-4602 — with Status screened/corpus placeholder and Claim links: none. Two non-canonical ledgers carry a WRONG one: full_text_queue_current.md names DOI 10.1038/onc.2010.222 and the journal Oncogene, and discovery_ledger_current.md names Oncogene. The same wrong DOI is in the study_id of the prior receipt FTR-20260814-20530675-01. The article is Cancer Research 2010;70(13):5577-86, confirmed independently from the JATS front matter and from the Europe PMC core record. reading_state.md and batch_queue.md carry the partial-read state, and surface_census.md lists the surface as structured/clean. No consolidated baseline claim is touched: the only canonical surface this reading bears on is the qualification note under CLAIM 036 (Status: in observation), which records juvenile osteosarcoma as conflicting across PAPER 057, 075 and 078.

retraction_check.result: CLEAN. PubMed efetch for PMID 20530675 on 2026-09-09 returns no CommentsCorrections element of any RefType — no retraction, no erratum, no expression of concern — and PublicationType carries only Journal Article plus three funding types. Journal and DOI were re-confirmed in the same call as Cancer research and 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-09-4602.

entries.proposition: The paper's central human prevalence datum: WWOX immunoreactivity is absent or reduced in 58% of 83 osteosarcoma specimens, against 0/12 normal bone and cartilage.
entries.snippet: In OS specimens, strong WWOX expression was detected in 42% (35/83), while 58% (48/83) exhibited absent or reduced (grouped as Altered) WWOX immunoreactivity
entries.anchor: Results, Frequent alteration of WWOX expression in human osteosarcoma (P14)

entries.proposition: The paper's headline mouse-penetrance claim, which revises the ~30% incidence of its own reference 7 upward to complete penetrance and is offered as the justification for the human study.
entries.snippet: Using this approach, 100% of Wwox-deficient mice had developed OS by 18 days-of-age and 68% of mice had bilateral involvement
entries.anchor: Results, High incidence of OS in Wwox-deficient mice (P13)

entries.proposition: An arithmetic error in the main text: 2/16 is 12.5%, not 22%. With this value the three chemotherapy categories in the same paragraph sum to 110%.
entries.snippet: WWOX decreased in post-chemotherapy specimens in 22% (2/16) of paired samples.

entries.proposition: The authors state in the Results that the inverse WWOX/RUNX2 association their Figure 5 title asserts is NOT present in the paired human cases.
entries.snippet: Although WWOX and RUNX2 results suggested an inverse association in human OSs, this was not evident when paired comparisons were performed on the 56 available cases
entries.anchor: Results, Aberrant RUNX2 expression in human osteosarcoma (P25)

entries.proposition: The authors record two osteosarcoma lines in which the inverse WWOX/RUNX2 relationship fails, inside the same paragraph that asserts it.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, the inverse correlation between WWOX and RUNX2 was not observed in two less differentiated OS cell lines, MG-63 and U2OS.
entries.anchor: Results, Loss of WWOX expression is associated with elevated RUNX2 levels (P23)

entries.proposition: The paper's selectivity inference — that WWOX restoration acts only where WWOX is lost — which rests entirely on a non-significant result in one cell line.
entries.snippet: Decreased tumorgenicity was not observed in K7M2 OS cells that express WWOX, suggesting that WWOX over-expression may not affect the cellular phenotype in WWOX-sufficient cells.

entries.proposition: After conceding the human correlation failed, the authors rescue the inverse relationship by appealing to an in vivo observation, and call it a correlation.
entries.snippet: although we did observe an inverse correlation in vivo in Wwox-deficient mice

entries.proposition: The xenograft group size, which bounds every tumour-volume comparison in Figure 3C including the K7M2 negative.
entries.snippet: into the flanks of 6-week-old female nude mice (Charles River Laboratories), five mice per group
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, In vivo studies (P9)

entries.proposition: The tumour-incidence result of the xenograft experiment is reported as data not shown; only mean volumes are displayed.
entries.snippet: 3 of 5 and 2 of 5 mice inoculated with Ad-WWOX-infected HOS cells and KHOS cells, respectively, displayed no tumors whereas all Ad-GFP-infected mice had tumors (data not shown)

entries.proposition: The significance statement for the soft-agar anchorage-independent growth result carries no relational operator in the deposited caption, so it cannot be read as P<0.001 without supplying a character the source does not contain.
entries.snippet: Columns, mean of triplicates samples; bars, SEM, (P 0.001).

entries.proposition: The Figure 5A caption asserts a specific between-line contrast in RUNX2 levels which the panel it describes does not show.
entries.snippet: HOS, Saos2 and KHOS (WWOX-reduced) cells have higher levels of RUNX2 compared to MC3T3 and K7M2 (Wwox-positive) cells.

entries.proposition: The Figure 1 caption points the normal-bone control at Supplemental Fig. 1, which is the microCT screening figure; the normal-tissue immunostain is Supplemental Fig. 2, as the Results text correctly states.
entries.snippet: H&E and WWOX immunostaining was uniformly strong in peribronchial cartilage and normal bone (400×) (see Supplemental Fig. 1)

entries.proposition: Table 1B's Total OS row prints a 95% confidence interval that lies entirely ABOVE its own point estimate of 43%. Recomputed by the paper's stated method (exact binomial), 56.60-88.54 is the interval for 24/32 — the positive count over the NEGATIVE count — while 24/56 gives 29.71-56.78.
The same denominator error in Table 1B's Resections row: 5.45-41.91 is the exact binomial interval for 4/21, the positives over the negatives, where 4/25 gives 4.54-36.08.
The stated interval method, against which both defective rows were recomputed and both correct rows reproduced exactly. The typographic errors are the source's own.
entries.snippet: 95% C.I. are based on exact binomail confidance interval

entries.proposition: The Figure S1 legend reports 19 of 22 knockout mice with tumours (86%), contradicting both the main text's 100% and Supplemental Table 1's 15+7=22. The bilateral fraction is quoted as 68.2% of 19 against Table 1's 68% of 22, so the percentages agree while the counts do not.
entries.snippet: Of 22 KO mice (ages 14-18 days), 19 had tumors (86% frequency)

entries.proposition: Supplemental Table 1's own footnote: three mice contributed a single imaged femur, so a bilateral score was not obtainable for them and the unilateral/bilateral split is not established for 3 of the 7 unilateral animals.
entries.snippet: indicates that only one femur was analyzed by microCT in 3 mice.

entries.proposition: The decisive cell of Supplemental Table 8: in pre-treatment biopsies WWOX-strong tumours are RUNX2-POSITIVE at 78%, i.e. the association runs in the same direction, not the inverse direction the Figure 5 title asserts.
entries.snippet: In primary tumor biopsies, 7/9 (78%) WWOX Strong tumors were also RUNX2 positive.

entries.proposition: The supplement states the negative outright: the inverse correlation suggested by the pooled data is absent when the cases are examined individually.
entries.snippet: Although the overall data in Table 1 suggested a possible inverse correlation, a correlation was not found when cases were examined in detail.

entries.proposition: A quantitative statement present only in the supplement and absent from the main text: every post-chemotherapy sample expressed WWOX, against 69% of pre-treatment samples.
entries.snippet: Overall, 16/16 (100%) of post-chemotherapy samples expressed WWOX

entries.proposition: The mouse femur Runx2 immunohistochemistry used a rabbit polyclonal antibody, which is not the monoclonal described in either the main or the supplementary Methods, and the only Runx2 secondary described there is anti-mouse.
entries.snippet: Femur sections from wild type and Wwox-deficient mice were stained with IgG (left panel) or polyclonal anti-Runx2 (M-70, Santa Cruz).

entries.proposition: The KHOS arm used a transduced POOL, not isolated clones, while the HOS arm used two isolated clones — so the main text's reference to KHOS-WWOX stable clones overstates the design.
entries.snippet: showing restoration of WWOX in KHOS pool clone

entries.snippet: P value was calculated relative to HOS-EV clone.

entries.proposition: PANEL SIDE, CONTRADICTING the Figure 5A caption: the two lines the caption places on the RUNX2-low side both carry clear RUNX2 bands, and the darkest band in the row belongs to a lane the paper names nowhere.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 5, panel A, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/nihms263536f5.jpg at its native 1050x779. The RUNX2 row runs across ten lanes labelled MCF7, MC3T3, K7M2, HOS, SAOS-2, MG-63, ROS, U2OS, KHOS, MDA-MB231. MC3T3 and K7M2 — the two lines the caption calls Wwox-positive and RUNX2-reduced — both carry distinct RUNX2 bands of intensity comparable to HOS, which the same caption places on the RUNX2-high side. The only essentially blank RUNX2 lane is MCF7, a breast line. ROS carries the darkest RUNX2 band in the row and is named neither in the caption nor in the Results paragraph. GAPDH is comparable across all ten lanes.
entries.contradicts_needle: have higher levels of RUNX2 compared to MC3T3 and K7M2

entries.proposition: PANEL SIDE, QUALIFYING the K7M2 selectivity inference: the panel neither confirms nor refutes it. K7M2 moves in the SAME direction as the responsive lines and is declared non-significant at n=5 with dispersion exceeding the mean, and the two control arms disagree with each other in opposite directions in the two responsive lines.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3, panel C, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/nihms263536f3.jpg at its native 1050x492 and re-read from a 300% crop. Three horizontal bar charts of tumour volume. KHOS: WWOX ~0.06, GFP ~0.62, Mock ~0.385, bracket drawn WWOX-to-GFP, P= 0.014*. HOS: WWOX ~0.005 with no visible bar, GFP ~0.26, MOCK ~0.50, bracket WWOX-to-GFP, P= 0.007**. K7M2: WWOX ~0.13, GFP ~0.265, MOCK ~0.20, P= 0.56. In KHOS the Mock bar is well BELOW the GFP bar; in HOS the MOCK bar is well ABOVE it. In K7M2 the WWOX mean is roughly half the GFP mean and the MOCK error bar extends to ~0.47, beyond twice its own mean.
entries.qualifies_needle: may not affect the cellular phenotype in WWOX-sufficient cells

entries.proposition: A discordance between WWOX mRNA and WWOX protein visible only by reading the two panels together, and an absent measurement: the one human osteosarcoma line with high WWOX mRNA is not on the protein blot at all.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2, panels A and C, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/nihms263536f2.jpg at its native 1050x284. Panel A bars are labelled with their values: hBM 1.00, MG-63 0.10, KHOS 0.09, SAOS2 0.45, HOSC-1 0.08, U2OS 0.70, MCF-7 0.74, MDAMB231 0.15. Panel C is an eight-lane blot: MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, MG-63, KHOS, K7M2, SAOS-2, HOS, MC3T3. SAOS-2 carries a barely detectable WWOX band despite the 0.45 mRNA value in panel A, while MCF-7 and MC3T3 carry strong bands. U2OS, the only human OS line with high mRNA (0.70), has no lane in panel C. The line called HOS everywhere else is labelled HOSC-1 in panel A.
entries.anchor: Figure 2, panels A and C, read at 1050x284

entries.proposition: The invasion result that the Discussion carries as suppressed migration and invasion is displayed as single percentages beside representative fields, with no dispersion and no replicate count in the panel.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 4, panels A-D, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/nihms263536f4.jpg at its native 1050x376. Panel A shows WWOX restored in clones CL11 and CL8 with GAPDH even. Panel B quantifies colonies for HOS ~25, HOS EV ~28 and HOS WWOX clone 11 ~8 — clone 8 is not quantified in this panel. Panel D is four stacked Matrigel fields labelled HOS 100%, HOS EV 92%, HOS WWOX CL11 60%, HOS WWOX CL8 60%, each a single percentage with no error bar and no n.

entries.proposition: Read from the pixels, the supplementary colony data show that the empty-vector control is itself far from the parental line, and that the two WWOX clones of the same construct differ from each other by about six-fold — so the effect size depends heavily on which clone and which control are chosen.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure S4, panels A-C, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/suppl_p16_FigS4.png, rendered from page 16 of the supplement PDF with pdftoppm -r 150. Panel B, colony number: HOS ~102, HOS EV ~60, HOS WWOX clone 11 ~8 marked P 0.002, HOS WWOX clone 8 ~48 marked P 0.037. The empty-vector control is roughly 59% of the parental line before any WWOX is introduced, and clone 8 sits at roughly 80% of that control while clone 11 sits at roughly 13% of it. Panel C, colony diameter: HOS ~1.35, HOS EV ~1.12, CL11 ~0.40 marked P 0.004, CL8 ~0.63 marked P 0.03. Panel A carries no parental HOS arm. All four printed P values carry no relational operator.
entries.anchor: Figure S4, panels A-C, supplement page 16 at 150 dpi

entries.proposition: The only in vivo evidence offered for the WWOX-RUNX2 relationship after the human correlation failed is a two-genotype immunostain in growth-plate cartilage, not in osteoblasts or tumour, with one unassigned negative control and no quantification.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure S6, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/suppl_p18_FigS6.png, rendered from page 18 of the supplement PDF with pdftoppm -r 150. Four panels arranged as Wwox WT (10X, 40X) above Wwox KO (10X, 40X), plus a single unlabelled panel captioned only 'control' at left. The stained tissue is epiphyseal growth-plate cartilage: columnar and hypertrophic chondrocytes in lacunae within a blue-counterstained cartilage matrix. Brown nuclear signal is visibly more intense and more frequent in the KO 40X panel than in the WT 40X panel. The single 'control' panel is not assigned to either genotype, so neither genotype has its own IgG control shown. No scale bar, no n, no scoring and no densitometry appear anywhere in the figure.
entries.anchor: Figure S6, supplement page 18 at 150 dpi

entries.proposition: The evidentiary display behind the complete-penetrance claim is one representative limb per genotype, with the lesion marked by a single arrow.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure S1, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/suppl_p13_FigS1.png, rendered from page 13 of the supplement PDF with pdftoppm -r 150. Panel A shows four microCT frames: WT whole femur (1) with a red box and its magnification (2), and KO whole femur (3) with a red box and its magnification (4). A single red arrow in frame 4 marks a bright irregularity on the cortical surface; the KO cortex is visibly thinner and more porous than the WT cortex in the paired magnifications. Panel B is a toluidine-blue section with two boxed regions expanded to BT, in which three black arrows label 'Tumor cells', and BN. One animal per genotype is displayed and no lesion count, size or quantification appears in the figure.
entries.anchor: Figure S1, panels A and B, supplement page 13 at 150 dpi

entries.proposition: The longitudinal within-patient observations — WWOX appearing after chemotherapy and disappearing in metastasis — are the strongest thing in the human arm and are visible in the pixels rather than only tabulated.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1, panels B and C, read from files/figures/PMID20530675/nihms263536f1.jpg at its native 1050x845. Panel B is three fields lettered i, j, k from one patient: j, the pre-chemotherapy WWOX immunostain, carries blue counterstain and essentially no chromogen, while k, the post-chemotherapy resection, carries dense brown chromogen. Panel C is three fields lettered l, m, n from one patient: m, the initial biopsy, is strongly brown, while n, the metastasis, is blue with essentially no chromogen. Panel A's four-column row shows the Normal, Strong, Reduced and Absent grades as panels b, d, f, h.
